message.content:
Upgrade the Nxeon server MIGRATION from "copy files + dump databases (no import), ask for DB password" into an automated LIFT-AND-SHIFT that migrates everything and brings it up running on the new server — in /opt/nxeon (Next.js 15, Prisma, tsx worker). The owner's requirements: (1) do NOT ask the customer for database passwords (they often don't know them) — we have root SSH, so dump databases using root/local auth; (2) detect and install PREREQUISITES on the target (e.g. Docker if the source runs containers, DB engines, web servers, runtimes); (3) everything should migrate and run as close as possible to how it ran on the old server.

## Study first (do NOT run git or `npm run build`)
- `worker/migrate-real.ts` — the HARDENED ssh2 transfer engine. READ the security model in full: strict allowlist validators that REJECT (never sanitize), secrets passed via files/STDIN never argv, per-migration work dir, secrets scrubbed in `finally`, timeouts. You must extend this WITHOUT weakening any of it.
- `worker/migrate-detect.ts` — the read-only scan (already detects web roots, home dirs, app dirs, Docker containers + mounts, listening ports, running services, DB engines). Reuse its findings.
- `worker/migrate.ts` (REAL_MIGRATION gate + SANDBOX simulation), `lib/actions-migrate.ts` (`scanSource`, `createMigration`, `CreateMigrationInput`, `MigrationItems`), `components/customer/MigrationWizard.tsx` (the wizard + the DB-password field to remove).

## SCHEMA CONSTRAINT
Do NOT edit `prisma/schema.prisma` (another agent owns it this wave). Carry any new migration options/results through the existing `Migration.items` Json column (extend the `MigrationItems` TS shape only). If you believe a schema field is unavoidable, STOP and note it — don't add one.

## CRITICAL SECURITY (unchanged bar)
Every command runs over SSH into an untrusted source AND writes onto the customer's target. Keep the exact injection-safe patterns: validate every interpolated value (hostnames, paths, db names, engine names, container/volume names, package names) against strict shell-inert allowlists before use; never interpolate an unvalidated value into a shell string; pass any secret via file/STDIN; bound everything with timeouts; confine work to the per-migration work dir. Re-validate anything that came back from the source scan before it is used in a command. Package installs on the target must use a fixed allowlist of package names (docker/compose, mysql/mariadb-server, postgresql, nginx, etc.) — never install an arbitrary source-provided string.

## Implement (extend migrate-real.ts + friends)
1. **Passwordless database migration.** Remove the customer DB-password requirement. On the SOURCE, dump databases using root's LOCAL access, best-effort, trying in order and logging which worked:
   - MySQL/MariaDB: `mysqldump --single-transaction --routines --triggers --all-databases` via the local root socket (Debian/Ubuntu root usually has `auth_socket`); write the dump into the work dir.
   - PostgreSQL: `sudo -u postgres pg_dumpall` (peer auth) into the work dir.
   If root can't authenticate to the engine (rare), log a clear, honest note and continue with the rest of the migration rather than failing the whole job. Then TRANSFER the dumps to the target and IMPORT them (install the engine first if missing): `mysql < dump.sql` as target root / `sudo -u postgres psql -f dumpall.sql`. Never echo DB contents to logs.
2. **Prerequisite install on the target**, derived from the scan (all from a FIXED package allowlist, idempotent, detect-then-install):
   - Docker containers detected → install Docker Engine + the compose plugin.
   - DB engines detected → install mysql/mariadb-server and/or postgresql.
   - nginx/apache configs or web roots detected → install the matching web server.
   - Runtimes detected from running app processes (node/python/etc.) → install a sane default (nodejs, python3+pip). Keep this conservative and logged.
3. **Docker replication.** Copy each detected compose project directory (the `docker-compose.yml`/`compose.yml` dirs) and each container's bind-mount host paths (already selected in the wizard) AND named-volume data (`/var/lib/docker/volumes/<name>/_data`) into the same locations on the target; then in each compose dir run `docker compose up -d` (fallback `docker-compose`). For standalone (non-compose) containers, log them with their `docker run`-equivalent (image + ports + mounts) so the user can recreate — attempt best-effort recreation only if trivially safe. Be honest in the log about what was auto-started vs. left for the user.
4. **App dirs & services.** Copy the selected app directories to the same paths. Where a running app maps to a simple systemd unit, copy/enable it best-effort; otherwise log the process + its cwd + command so the user can re-enable it. Copy web-server vhost configs + enable sites where safe.
5. **Bring-up + verification.** After transfer/import/up, verify: DB engines running, `docker ps` shows the expected containers, and the previously-detected listening ports are now listening on the target. Write a clear per-step result into the migration log and a final summary of "migrated & running" vs "copied — needs manual step".
6. **Wizard changes** (`MigrationWizard.tsx` + `actions-migrate`): remove the DB-password inputs entirely; databases are auto-included when an engine is detected (show "Databases (MySQL/Postgres) — included automatically, no password needed"). Show the prerequisites that will be installed on the target ("We'll install Docker + compose, MySQL…") and set honest expectations ("We migrate and start everything we can; anything that needs a manual step is listed at the end"). Keep the pre-checked app/web/docker selections.

## Honesty requirement
Do NOT claim a container/app is "running identically" unless the bring-up + verification actually confirmed it. The final migration summary must distinguish what was verified-running from what was copied-but-needs-attention. A best-effort step that fails must log the reason and NOT fail the whole migration.

## SANDBOX
Update the simulation so staging shows the richer flow (dumping DBs via root, installing Docker/compose + engines on target, importing DBs, `compose up`, verification) with synthetic success — no real SSH.

## Constraints
- No new npm deps (`ssh2` available). No schema change (extend `MigrationItems` TS only). Do NOT touch mail/signature, billing, resize, terminal, cpanel, backup files. Do NOT run git or `npm run build`.
- Write/Edit may time out on a hook — fall back to Bash heredocs and verify.
- Verify ONLY with `cd /opt/nxeon && npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | grep -v "test/.*test.ts"` (clean for your files).

Report: how passwordless DB dump/import works (+ fallback), the prerequisite install allowlist + logic, the Docker/compose + named-volume replication + bring-up, the verification step, the wizard changes (DB password removed), and exactly what is auto-run vs left-for-user — plus a frank note on the limits of "runs exactly as before".

## Summary

I turned the migration from "copy files + dump DBs (no import), ask for DB password" into an automated **passwordless lift-and-shift** that installs prerequisites, copies to the same paths, imports databases, brings Docker/services up, and verifies — extending `worker/migrate-real.ts`, `worker/migrate.ts`, `worker/migrate-detect.ts`, `lib/actions-migrate.ts`, and `components/customer/MigrationWizard.tsx`. No schema change (everything rides on `Migration.items`); no new deps.

### Passwordless DB dump/import (+ fallback)
On the SOURCE, over the existing sshpass/ssh channel, using root's **local** auth (no password ever collected):
- MySQL/MariaDB: `mysqldump --single-transaction --routines --triggers --events --all-databases` (socket/`auth_socket`).
- PostgreSQL: `sudo -u postgres pg_dumpall` (peer auth). A `sudo -n ` prefix is added automatically when the SSH user isn't root.

Dumps stream to files under the per-migration work dir (never echoed to logs). On the TARGET they import as our own root: `mysql < dump` / `sudo -u postgres psql -f dump`. **Fallback/honesty:** if root can't authenticate to an engine, or import fails, it logs a clear reason, keeps the dump under `/root/nxeon-migrations/<id>/dumps` for manual retry, and continues — it never fails the whole job.

### Prerequisite install allowlist + logic
`ensurePackages()` — detect-then-install, idempotent, best-effort per package, from a FIXED compile-time allowlist only (never a source string). Keys → apt strings (dnf/yum fallback): `docker` (`docker.io docker-compose-plugin`), `mysql` (`mariadb-server`), `postgresql`, `nginx`, `apache` (`apache2`/`httpd`), `nodejs` (`nodejs npm`), `python3` (`python3 python3-pip`). Selected from the scan: DB engines present → DB servers; containers present → Docker+compose; nginx/apache seen (or web roots) → web server; node/python app runtimes → runtimes. Engines/docker are then `systemctl enable --now`'d.

### Docker/compose + named-volume replication + bring-up
Selected paths (incl. bind mounts and compose dirs) rsync to the **same absolute paths** on the target. Named volumes → `docker volume create <name>` + rsync `/var/lib/docker/volumes/<name>/_data`. Each copied compose dir runs `docker compose up -d` (fallback `docker-compose`). Standalone (non-compose) containers are **logged** with their image+ports+mounts run-equivalent (never auto-`docker run` of an arbitrary source image). Best-effort systemd unit copy+enable and nginx/apache vhost copy+`nginx -t`/`apachectl configtest`+reload.

### Verification
After bring-up: DB engines `systemctl is-active`/`pgrep`; `docker ps -q | wc -l`; and each previously-listening port checked with `ss -lnt`. Each check is recorded as verified-**running** vs **copied** (needs attention).

### Wizard changes (DB password removed)
Removed both DB credential inputs and the per-database checklist. Databases now show "included automatically, no password needed"; a panel lists prerequisites ("We'll install Docker + Compose, MySQL…"); expectations set honestly ("We migrate and start everything we can; anything needing a manual step is listed at the end"). Pre-checked app/web/docker selections kept. `scanSource` no longer receives DB creds; `createMigration` derives the whole plan server-side from the scan.

### Auto-run vs left-for-user
Auto-run & verified where confirmed: prerequisite installs, DB import, `compose up`, simple systemd services (copied+active), vhost reload, listening ports. Left for the user (logged, not failed): standalone non-compose containers, any DB that root couldn't dump/import, compose/service/vhost steps that didn't come up cleanly, and ports not yet listening.

### Frank note on "runs exactly as before"
It won't always be byte-identical. Compose namespaces named volumes by project, so pre-seeded volumes only line up when names match; distro package versions differ from the source; DB engine variants (MySQL vs MariaDB) and custom-compiled/non-simple systemd units may not restart cleanly; and standalone containers are deliberately not auto-run. That's why the final summary and completion notice explicitly separate "migrated & running (verified)" from "copied — needs a manual step" rather than claiming parity.
